arxiv-1804-08373.title: Bisimulations for Delimited-Control Operators Thanks: This work was supported by PHC Polonium and by National Science Centre, Poland, grant no. 2014/15/B/ST6/00619.
arxiv-1804-08373.creator: Dariusz Biernacki \rsuper a, Sergueï Lenglet \rsuper b, Piotr Polesiuk \rsuper a
arxiv-1804-08373.description: Abstract . We present a comprehensive study of the behavioral theory of an untyped λ \lambda -calculus extended with the delimited-control operators 𝗌𝗁𝗂𝖿𝗍 \mathsf{shift} and 𝗋𝖾𝗌𝖾𝗍 \mathsf{reset} . To that end, we define a contextual equivalence for this calculus, that we then aim to characterize with coinductively defined relations, called bisimilarities .

arxiv-2106-06188.title: Precise large deviations of sums of widely dependent random variables and its applications
arxiv-2106-06188.creator: Zhaolei Cui and Yuebao Wang 1 School of mathematics and statistics, Changshu Institute of Technology, Suzhou 215000, China2 School of Mathematical Sciences, Soochow University, Suzhou 215006, China
arxiv-2106-06188.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Zhaolei Cui and Yuebao Wang 1 School of mathematics and statistics, Changshu Institute of Technology, Suzhou 215000, China2 School of Mathematical Sciences, Soochow University, Suzhou 215006, China. Abstract In this paper, we obtain some results on precise large deviations for non-random and random sums of widely dependent random variables with common dominatedly varying tail distribution or consistently varying tail distribution on (-\infty,\infty) .

arxiv-2111-00393.title: Chow rings of matroids are Koszul
arxiv-2111-00393.creator: Matthew Mastroeni, Jason McCullough
arxiv-2111-00393.description: Abstract . Chow rings of matroids were instrumental in the resolution of the Heron-Rota-Welsh Conjecture by Adiprasito, Huh, and Katz and in the resolution of the Top-Heavy Conjecture by Braden, Huh, Matherne, Proudfoot, and Wang. The Chow ring of a matroid is a commutative, graded, Artinian, Gorenstein algebra with linear and quadratic relations defined by the matroid.

arxiv-2203-13470.title: Interactive Style Transfer: All is Your Palette
arxiv-2203-13470.creator: Zheng Lin, Zhao Zhang, Kang-Rui Zhang, Bo Ren, Ming-Ming Cheng
arxiv-2203-13470.description: Abstract Neural style transfer (NST) can create impressive artworks by transferring reference style to content image. Current image-to-image NST methods are short of fine-grained controls, which are often demanded by artistic editing. To mitigate this limitation, we propose a drawing-like interactive style transfer (IST) method, by which users can interactively create a harmonious-style image.

arxiv-2205-08858.title: Tight Differential Privacy Guarantees for the Shuffle Model with k k -Randomized Response
arxiv-2205-08858.creator: Sayan Biswas, Kangsoo Jung, Catuscia Palamidessi
arxiv-2205-08858.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Sayan Biswas, Kangsoo Jung, Catuscia Palamidessi. Most differentially private algorithms assume a central model in which a reliable third party inserts noise to queries made on datasets, or a local model where the data owners directly perturb their data. However, the central model is vulnerable via a single point of failure, and the local model has the disadvantage that the utility of the data deteriorates significantly. The recently proposed shuffle model is an intermediate framework between the central and local paradigms.

arxiv-2209-12530.title: On some Frobenius type divisibility results in a premodular category
arxiv-2209-12530.creator: Sebastian Burciu
arxiv-2209-12530.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Sebastian Burciu. Abstract In this note some new Frobenius type divisibility results are obtained for premodular categories. In particular, we extend [ Yu20 , Corollary 3.4] from the settings of super-modular categories to arbitrary pseudo-unitary premodular categories. Introduction In [ Yu20 ] the author showed that in a slightly-degenerate braided fusion category one has that \frac{\dim(\mathcal{C})}{2\dim(Y)^{2}}\in\mathbb{A} for any simple object Y of \mathcal{C} .

arxiv-2310-05014.title: Congruence Closure Modulo Groups Thanks: This research is supported by the Austrian Science Fund (FWF) project I 5943.
arxiv-2310-05014.creator: Dohan Kim ORCID:0000-0003-1973-615X
arxiv-2310-05014.description: Abstract . This paper presents a new framework for constructing congruence closure of a finite set of ground equations over uninterpreted symbols and interpreted symbols for the group axioms. In this framework, ground equations are flattened into certain forms by introducing new constants, and a completion procedure is performed on ground flat equations.

arxiv-2405-02630.title: Validating Large-Scale Quantum Machine Learning: Efficient Simulation of Quantum Support Vector Machines Using Tensor Networks
arxiv-2405-02630.creator: Kuan-Cheng Chen, Tai-Yue Li, Yun-Yuan Wang, Simon See, Chun-Chieh Wang, Robert Wille, Nan-Yow Chen, An-Cheng Yang, Chun-Yu Lin
arxiv-2405-02630.description: Abstract We present an efficient tensor-network-based approach for simulating large-scale quantum circuits exemplified by Quantum Support Vector Machines (QSVMs). Experimentally, leveraging the cuTensorNet library on multiple GPUs, our method effectively reduces the exponential runtime growth to near-quadratic scaling with respect to the number of qubits in practical scenarios.

arxiv-2411-13738.title: Assessing Gender Bias in LLMs: Comparing LLM Outputs with Human Perceptions and Official Statistics
arxiv-2411-13738.creator: Tetiana Bas
arxiv-2411-13738.description: Abstract This study investigates gender bias in large language models (LLMs) by comparing their gender perception to that of human respondents, U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics data, and a 50% no-bias benchmark. We created a new evaluation set using occupational data and role-specific sentences.

arxiv-2507-09038.title: A Phase-field Model for Apoptotic Cell Death
arxiv-2507-09038.creator: Daniel A. Vaughan 1,2 , Anna M. Piccinini 2 , Mischa Zelzer 2 , Etienne Farcot 1 , Bindi S. Brook 1 , Kris Van-der-Zee 1 , and Luis Espath 1
arxiv-2507-09038.description: Abstract . The process of programmed cell death, namely apoptosis, is a natural mechanism that regulates healthy tissue, multicellular structures, and homeostasis. An improved understanding of apoptosis can significantly enhance our knowledge of biological processes and systems. For instance, pathogens can manipulate the apoptotic process to either evade immune detection or to facilitate their spread.

arxiv-2509-02576.title: B rück conjecture for solutions of first-order partial differential equations in ℂ m \mathbb{C}^{m} Thanks: Typeset by AmS- L a T e X
arxiv-2509-02576.creator: Sujoy Majumder, Nabadwip Sarkar and Debabrata Pramanik
arxiv-2509-02576.description:
A 2025 arXiv research paper by Sujoy Majumder, Nabadwip Sarkar and Debabrata Pramanik. In the paper, we consider Brück conjecture as the solutions of first-order partial differential equations in several complex variables. Our results ensure that Brück conjecture in ℂ m \mathbb{C}^{m} is valid under some additional conditions. In pursuit of this goal, we have also established the Borel-Caratheodory theorem in ℂ m \mathbb{C}^{m} and derived several fundamental results concerning order and hyper-order into higher dimensions. †

arxiv-2509-09469.title: Resource-Efficient Glioma Segmentation on Sub-Saharan MRI
arxiv-2509-09469.creator: Freedmore Sidume, Oumayma Soula, Joseph Muthui Wacira, YunFei Zhu, Abbas Rabiu Muhammad, Abderrazek Zeraii, Oluwaseun Kalejaye, Hajer Ibrahim, Olfa Gaddour, Brain Halubanza, Dong Zhang Udunna C Anazodo Confidence Raymond
arxiv-2509-09469.description: Abstract Gliomas are the most prevalent type of primary brain tumors, and their accurate segmentation from MRI is critical for diagnosis, treatment planning, and longitudinal monitoring. However, the scarcity of high-quality annotated imaging data in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) poses a significant challenge for deploying advanced segmentation models in clinical workflows.

pmc-10595799.creator: R Pasupathy, R Sazevari, C Queen
pmc-10595799.description: BackgroundThe population in the Baltic nations of Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania is ageing rapidly. Technology is a potential resource in enhancing the health and wellbeing of the elderly. The use of technology reduces social isolation through the facilitation of communication and facilitates access to healthcare resources.

pmc-11333631.title: Germ aversion is a risk factor for chronic low back pain and shoulder pain under the COVID-19 pandemic: an internet-based panel study
pmc-11333631.creator: Yuki Mashima, Morihiko Kawate, Yihuan Wu, Yuta Shinohara, Reiko Hoshino, Saki Takaoka, Chisato Tanaka, Masahito Tokita, Akihito Shimazu, Kenta Wakaizumi
pmc-11333631.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The COVID-19 pandemic has increased germ aversion, an aversive affective response to a high likelihood of pathogen transmission. While psychological factors are associated with chronic pain, the relationship between germ aversion and chronic pain remains unexplored. This study aimed to examine the relationship between germ aversion and new-onset and prognosis of chronic pain using longitudinal data collected during the COVID-19 pandemic. We conducted web-based surveys of full-time workers at baseline and after three months.

pmc-11690914.title: CREATION AND EVALUATION OF A VIDEO SERIES SHARING A PALLIATIVE APPROACH TO CARE IN CANADIAN LONG-TERM CARE HOMES
pmc-11690914.creator: Abigail Wickson-Griffiths, Paulette Hunter, Susan Tupper, Allison Cammer, Sharon Kaasalainen, Tamara Sussman
pmc-11690914.description: Video-assisted patient education is a favored format for accessing healthcare information. Based on a consultative process, the purpose of this project was to create and evaluate a video education resource to support communication between staff and family caregivers in Canadian long-term care (LTC) homes when introducing a palliative approach to care.

pmc-12572383.title: Implication of an exosome-based gene signature for estimating clinical outcomes of triple-negative breast cancer and assisting in individualized therapy
pmc-12572383.creator: Qiong Yang, Xufan Cai, Yangyang Qian, Tianyao Yang, Wenjie Xia, Miaochun Zhong, Zaiyuan Ye
pmc-12572383.description: Exosomes play a crucial role in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), influencing various aspects of tumor progression. Given the importance of exosomes in TNBC biology, we proposed a novel exosome-based model that was critically implicated in TNBC. Bulk and single-cell transcriptomics and genetic mutations of TNBC patients were curated for our study.

pmc-12574617.title: Real‐World Effectiveness of Nirsevimab in Preventing RSV Hospitalizations: Evidence of Protection in Southern Italian Infants, 2024–2025
pmc-12574617.creator: Francesca Fortunato, Rosa Prato, Angelo Acquafredda, Angelo Campanozzi, Valeria Delli Carri, Rosa Francavilla, Giuseppina Iannelli, Pio Liberatore, Gianfranco Maffei, Matteo Mariano, Loris Micelli, Marilena Nesta, Maria Rosa Pastore, Annamaria Calvo, Matteo Rinaldi, Pier Luigi Lopalco, Domenico Mart
pmc-12574617.description: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of hospitalization in infants, resulting in millions of cases and hundreds of thousands of deaths worldwide every year. Nirsevimab, a long‐acting monoclonal antibody approved in 2023, has 75%–90% protection against RSV‐related admissions. This study evaluated the effectiveness of nirsevimab in preventing RSV‐hospitalization among infants in southern Italy during 2024–2025 season.

pmc-12649573.title: Approach–Avoidance Conflict Paradigms in Animal and Human Studies of Anxiety—A Narrative Review
pmc-12649573.creator: Shijie Liu, Ziqiang Xin, Huiwen Xiao
pmc-12649573.description: Anxiety disorders are among the most prevalent mental health conditions worldwide, yet their assessment and treatment have long been limited by insufficient validity. To address this challenge, researchers have increasingly sought to translate approach–avoidance conflict paradigms from animal models into human experimental tasks.

pmc-12705754.title: Data driven pedagogy in physical education a new paradigm in teaching effectiveness
pmc-12705754.creator: Yongfu Wu
pmc-12705754.description: The standard practice of physical education (PE) teaching relies primarily on traditional pedagogical methods that lack systematic data-based techniques for measuring teaching performance. A flexible systematic approach becomes vital because students’ learning styles, performance dynamics, and teaching targets create fluid teaching conditions. A unified teaching-decision-making structure emerges to boost physical education effectiveness through the presented approach.
